How do I start the assessment?: Click a mode card (Quick Check or Deep Dive) on the Welcome screen, or Start Assessment in the minibar. You'll fill in your organisation profile, then answer domain questions.
What is Quick Check vs Deep Dive?: Quick Check samples 2 questions per domain (18 total across 9 domains, ~15 min). Deep Dive asks up to 6 questions per domain (~45 min) for full control-level granularity, and is required for certification-ready output.
How do I upload evidence?: Open the Supplier Evidence tab, click Add File, select a PDF, DOCX or image (max 1MB), and choose a document category. A thumbnail preview is shown and you can download the original later.
How do I change risk multipliers?: Open the Risk Settings tab in your results (not the Admin Settings gear icon), adjust the Region/Sector/Size sliders (1.00-1.30x), then click Apply Settings. Use Reset to Defaults to undo.
What is the AI Ask toolbar?: It's the AI Ask button in the header - a chat panel where you can ask how to use the tool or ask security questions. It uses live AI if you've set an API key, otherwise it answers from this offline FAQ.
How do I generate the PDF report?: Click the Download PDF button on the results screen. It produces a 3-page report: cover + scores + AI summary, domain table + top gaps, and roadmap + financial breakdown + sign-off box.
What is CyberScore?: CyberScore (0-100, higher is better) measures your security control maturity, calculated as a weighted average across all 9 domains (IAM 0.15, Detection 0.14, Network 0.13, Cloud/Data/Governance/People 0.12 each, Supply Chain 0.10, Policy Review 0.10).
What is Risk Score?: Risk Score (0-100, lower is better) = (100 - CyberScore) x sector/region/size risk multipliers. It reflects your exposure level: Low, Medium, High, or Critical.
What is Cost of Inaction?: Cost of Inaction is your Annualised Loss Expectancy (ALE) - the expected yearly financial loss from a breach, based on a FAIR risk model using your revenue and risk score.
What does ALE mean?: ALE = Annualised Loss Expectancy. It's calculated as Single Loss Expectancy (SLE) x Annual Rate of Occurrence (ARO) - the expected cost of a breach per year.
What does SLE mean?: SLE = Single Loss Expectancy - the estimated financial loss from one breach event, roughly 12-18% of annual revenue in this model.
What does ARO mean?: ARO = Annual Rate of Occurrence - how many times a given loss event is expected to happen per year, based on your risk score.
What do the dots A to F mean in the Risk: Each dot is a specific threat scenario (Ransomware, Phishing, Insider threat, Supply chain, Data breach, Cloud misconfiguration) plotted by likelihood and business impact. Check the legend under the matrix for the full A-F mapping, or hover a dot to see its name.
What is the Optimiser?: The Optimiser tab lets you set a budget, timeframe, risk capacity, and optimisation objective (cost, speed, or compliance) to get a prioritised remediation plan, with a Do Nothing comparison mode.
How do I generate a Board Report?: Open the Roadmap tab and click Generate Board Report under the AI Board Report card - it needs an API key (or Demo mode) to produce a one-page board-ready summary.
What is the Gap Register?: The Gap Register tab lists prioritised security gaps by severity, with estimated cost, risk reduction, and mapped controls (ISO/NIST/CIS references). Filter by severity or Five Eyes-related items.
Where is my data stored?: Everything - your answers, context, and history - is stored only in your browser's local storage. Nothing is uploaded to a server. Clearing your browser data or switching devices will lose it, so export a PDF if you need a permanent copy.
What happens if I close the browser or l: Your answers are saved to local storage as you move between domains, so reopening the same browser lets you resume via the Resume Assessment in Progress button on the Welcome screen.
What certifications does the tool suppor: 12+ frameworks including Cyber Essentials, ISO 27001, NIST CSF 2.0, DORA, NIS2, SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, CIS Controls, IASME, FCA SYSC, and the Five Eyes AI & Cyber Resilience statement - auto-filtered by your selected region and sector.
How do I enable AI features?: Open Admin Settings (gear icon, default password cyberscore2026) or the My AI Settings card on the Welcome screen, choose Gemini or Claude, and paste your API key.
Why does my assessment already have answ: This can happen if you viewed the Demo just before starting a real assessment. Use Start Assessment from the Welcome screen to begin a clean session - it clears any demo data automatically.
What is a CyberScore band?: Bands describe your maturity level: Critical (0-20), Developing (21-40), Established (41-60), Advanced (61-80), Leading (81-100).
How is the peer benchmark calculated?: Peer benchmark is an average CyberScore for your selected industry sector, used to show how your domain scores compare (+/- vs peer) on the dashboard and PDF report.
What currencies are supported?: GBP, EUR, and USD. Switch currency from Admin Settings - all figures update using the current exchange rate, though internal calculations are always stored in GBP.
Who can see my assessment?: No one - it's entirely local to your browser. Use the PDF export or History tab export if you need to share results with a colleague.
What is the difference between Admin Set: Admin Settings (gear icon, password protected) configures the app globally: AI provider/key, currency, demo mode, and admin password. Risk Settings is a tab inside an active assessment for adjusting region/sector/size risk multipliers for that specific assessment.
